paper.title: AgentDevel: Reframing Self-Evolving LLM Agents as Release Engineering
paper.central_claim: AgentDevel: agent improvement is reframed as release engineering. A single canonical agent line is improved by an implementation-blind LLM critic, script-based executable diagnosis and one release candidate per iteration promoted under flip-centred (pass->fail / fail->pass) gating, yielding stable improvements with fewer regressions than in-agent self-refinement or population search.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref null: not exposed to the worker by the configured model type; no extra probing per controller instruction.

evidence.quote: agents are treated as shippable artifacts, and improvement is externalized into a regression-aware release pipeline.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim: externalised, regression-aware release pipeline for agent improvement.

evidence.quote: Importantly, the critic does not perform causal attribution and does not propose repairs.
evidence.support_explanation: Critic is implementation-blind and symptom-level only; repairs come from a separate synthesis step.

evidence.quote: Diagnostic scripts are regenerated at each iteration, but they are allowed to reference scripts from the previous iteration.
evidence.support_explanation: Diagnosis scripts are re-written each iteration with previous scripts as soft references (a mildly evolving inspection routine).

evidence.quote: These updates may involve any part of the blueprint—prompt, code, or tool wrappers—and are bundled into a single, unified change package.
evidence.support_explanation: RC synthesis: one bundled edit over prompt/code/tool wrappers; no edit localisation or edit budget.

evidence.quote: Gating as release acceptance on the same TrainSet.
evidence.support_explanation: Gate is evaluated on the same development set that generated the RC.

evidence.quote: We emphasize that AgentDevel does not prescribe a universal set of thresholds; rather, it provides the evidence (flip sets, rates, and symptom-aligned summaries) that the gate uses to make a release-style decision.
evidence.support_explanation: Gate function G and thresholds are not specified, so accept/reject is not reproducible from the text.

gap.author_gap: Self-improvement inside the agent or search over many variants gives unstable, hard-to-audit trajectories, making non-regression and failure reasoning across versions hard; aggregate scores hide per-example regressions.
gap.checked_gap: Real engineering concern (regressions masked by averages), but the paper shows no measurement that neighbours suffer from it in the same setting, and validation-gated acceptance of edits is a standard element of prompt/scaffold optimisers (not discussed). The 'root issue is partly a matter of framing' claim is argumentative.

gap.residue: Regression behaviour of rivals under the same base agent and budget; out-of-sample (test) regression measurement.
gap.stakes: Production reliability: bad releases that break working cases.
gap.method_response: Single line + per-example flip gate + executable diagnosis + blind critic.
gap.remaining_gap: Held-out non-regression not measured; gate thresholds, base agent and split sizes unspecified; no rival comparison.

G.reason: Real practical concern and named neighbours, but the framing is largely argumentative: no measurement of neighbours' regressions, and validation-gated acceptance used by existing optimisers is not discussed; remaining gap boundary is thin.

M.reason: Pipeline is sensible and the blind-critic/executable-diagnosis separation is reasoned, but the central objective (non-regression) is checked only on the set that generates edits, the RC synthesis function is a black box, and edit scope is unconstrained.

X.reason: Version line, discard-on-reject and saved artifacts are described, but the gate decision rule, thresholds, stopping values, hit-rate/FTP/P2P definitions, base agent and per-benchmark protocol are missing; rejection of iteration 11 contradicts the stated rationale.

E.measurement.reason: Primary metrics use standard programmatic verifiers (tests, benchmark scorers); critic-based judgement is only a fallback. Internal table inconsistencies are noted but do not invalidate the verifiers.

E.causality.reason: Ablations are single-run on one benchmark with 1-2 point test differences; the ungated variant tests higher; a strong improver (Claude Code) on a weak b0 is a competing explanation and no rival improver or equal-budget naive 'iterate on train' control is run; superiority claims against search/self-refinement are untested.

E.holdout.reason: Test set is declared single-use and separate, but sizes, disjointness, prior exposure of the base model to these benchmarks and whether ablation variants share the split are unreported; the non-regression claim is made in-sample and the train-test gap is large (78.5 vs 34.2).

E.statistics.reason: Single run per setting, no intervals, no sizes, small ablation margins; flip counts per iteration and rejected iterations are shown for one benchmark.

E.cost.reason: Only a qualitative overhead limitation; iteration and reject counts exist for StableToolBench and a reject rate in Table 3, but no tokens, dollars, time or budget parity with rivals.
